title: Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaona
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Vayikra Rabbah 5:2 has Rabbi Levi reporting in his name. Hyman reports that Bereshit Rabbah 91:8 reads bar Shaula and that the Arukh, under Bar Hadya, reads bar Shechina. He cites Seder HaDorot’s identification with R' Chana Shaona of Avodah Zarah 75a.

notes.text: The supplied Tana Shaona form remains a source question; it is not silently changed to a conjectured personal name. Shaona, Shaula and Shechina are preserved as different forms.

The saved whole TE VayikraRabbah5:2 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Levi reporting Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaona and the bar-hadya bird. It supports those exact titles and explains the lexical context, but is not an independently inspected Arukh witness. Shaona, Shaula and Shechina remain distinct readings; finite BereshitRabbah/AZ searches do not establish universal absence. SederHaDorot’s proposed identification with R' Tana Shaona is attributed to that work, not admitted as identity or a Tanna-generation conclusion.

Printed Hyman (vol. II, p. 686) cites Bereshit Rabbah 91:8 and reads Chana Shaona where the supplied transcription has Tana. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 91:8 reads bar Sheilah in Rabbi Levi’s report about Joseph. The digital Arukh entry “Bar Hadya” quotes Rabbi Levi reporting Yochanan bar Shechina and records a further variant, bar Chirya. Seder HaDorot tentatively connects the names. Avodah Zarah 75a reads Chana Sheinah or bar Sheinah, while the parallel in Niddah 65b reads Chanah Shauna or bar Shauna. Both passages report the half-day and half-night ruling through Rabbah bar bar Chanah in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. The witnesses document distinct forms and leave the proposed identity open.
